passages.text: An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.
Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Timeless Body

You served as a healer during one of Aethel's many conflicts, tending to the wounded and dying on blood-soaked battlefields. You've developed nerves of steel, quick hands, and an intimate knowledge of trauma and recovery. Now you bring those skills to the adventuring life, whether seeking redemption, escape from memories, or new ways to help others.
Skill Proficiencies: Medicine, Insight
Tool Proficiencies: Healer's kit, Herbalism kit
Equipment: A healer's kit, a bloodstained bandana or token from your service, a journal containing medical notes and sketches, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 gp.

Feature: Trauma Response: Your battlefield experience has honed your emergency medical skills. When you use a healer's kit to stabilize a dying creature, they regain 1 hit point immediately. Additionally, you can identify the nature and severity of injuries at a glance. Your service grants you Liked starting Reputation with veterans of the conflict you served in but Neutral starting Reputation with those who fought on the opposing side.
| Healer's kit | 5 gp | 3 lb. |
| Rations (1 day) | 5 sp | 2 lb. |
| Cook's utensils | 1 gp | 8 lb. |
14. Soulrender
Overview: A necrotic engine of agony who harvests souls to power abilities, damage enemies, or shield allies.
Requirements:
Base Class: Mage, Crimson Agent, or Cleric (Lv 10+)
Feats: Lifeleech, Soul Cage, Wounding Magic
Skills: Arcana, Religion, Intimidation
Unlock: Steal the soul of a living named enemy and bind it to a black crystal during a ritual event.
Signature Mechanics:
Soul Harvest: Absorb the soul of a dying foe to gain energy
Agony Lance: Fire a necrotic beam that deals damage over time and weakens saves

ordinarySpellSources.name: Stitch Fate

operational.targets: One living dying creature at 0 HP you can perceive within range and line of effect. Dead and Stable creatures are ineligible.
operational.resolution: Choose one mode before paying. Unravel Failure requires at least one recorded failed death save and removes one failure. Stitch Life clears death-save counters and restores 1 HP as direct state recovery.
operational.effect: Unravel Failure leaves the creature dying at 0 HP with its other recorded successes/failures intact. Stitch Life restores a living dying creature to 1 HP, ending its zero-HP dying state. If a broad cannot-regain-HP effect blocks that 1 HP, instead clear its death counters, make it Stable at 0, and roll its ordinary d4-hour recovery deadline from now. A still-active HP prohibition can defer that eventual recovery; damage or death cancels it normally.
operational.scaling: None. The spell changes only one recorded failure or the defined 1-HP state recovery.
operational.limitations: An Action cannot interrupt or retroactively change a completed death. This is not resurrection or ordinary HP healing; ordinary healing bonuses/halves do not alter the 1-HP state value. It removes no Wounds, Corruption, class Curse, conditions, debt or spent-resource consequences. Normal class access, RP, Dissonance, Refrain, components and countering rules apply. No refund after a legally paid cast is countered or fails at resolution.
operational.designNotes: Core Divination rank8, 21RP, Action, 120ft, V/S/F and Instantaneous are preserved. Source says change one failed death save or auto-revive a dying target. NEW: two explicit modes; recorded-failure removal instead of a retroactive reroll; living-dying eligibility; 1-HP state recovery and blocked-recovery Stable bridge. Reviewed operational playtest overlay; provisional design decisions remain labeled NEW.

ordinarySpellSources.name: Resurrection

operational.targets: One willing dead creature whose sufficiently intact remains are within range and line of effect, and whose death occurred no more than 8 elapsed hours ago
operational.resolution: No attack or save. Check the dead identity's willingness, sufficient body, exact elapsed death window, location and actual resurrection/soul blockers. On a legal successful resolution, return that identity to life at 1 HP.
operational.effect: Change Dead to Living, assign 1 returned HP, clear death-save counters and any previous Stable recovery deadline. Preserve Wounds, Corruption, Oracle Curse, other persistent death consequences and spent resources. This returned HP is a resurrection state transition, not ordinary healing; ordinary healing reductions and generic living HP-gain prohibitions do not change it. Explicit resurrection or soul blockers prevent return.
operational.scaling: None. One identity returns at 1 HP; no additional targets or restored resources.
operational.limitations: Does not create a missing viable body, duplicate a creature, compel an unwilling return, bypass a real planar/soul barrier, clear lethal tracks or repair otherwise lethal persistent afflictions. After successful return, retain Exhaustion6/Expedition6 and enter their protected living-collapse states. Later positive unprevented gain is lethal again; qualifying care and point gates still apply. This candidate remains reviewed for the operational playtest overlay. Known illegal prerequisites prevent activation; a legal cast already paid receives no refund for a later refusal, counter or changed eligibility. Normal RP, Dissonance, Refrain and component rules apply.
operational.designNotes: Core Necromancy rank7, 17RP, Action, 120ft, V/S/F and Instantaneous retained. Class gates remain Cleric/Druid/Wizard13 and Shaman19. operational.effect: Return the one identity to life at1HP, clearing death-save counters and any former Stable recovery deadline. Any other remains of this identity lose eligibility to create a second living instance; they remain mundane remains/history evidence as appropriate. No equipment, resources or second creature are created from duplicate remains.
operational.scaling: None. One creature at1HP, with no restored class resources.

Lethal tracks and persistent afflictions remain; apply their reviewed reconciliation rather than silently removing them. Refusal or a counter after a legal paid activation refunds nothing. Normal spell risk and component rules apply.

ordinarySpellSources.name: Soul Bind

operational.targets: One living dying creature at0HP you can perceive within range and line of effect; a Dead or Stable creature is ineligible
operational.duration: Pending tether up to1 minute; if target dies while pending, bound identity for24 elapsed hours from that death
operational.resolution: Target makes a Charisma save against your spell save DC. On success no effect. On failure create a pending Soul Bind tether with an absolute expiry60 seconds after resolution. Target death before that expiry converts it into one soul-bound identity record with expiry24 hours after the death.
operational.effect: Before death, gaining positiveHP or becoming Stable ends the pending tether. After conversion, that identity cannot return by resurrection until the24-hour record ends or a legally capable source removes it. Neither state requires concentration or ends merely because a caster dies/incapacitates. If death begins at or after the pending absolute expiry, conversion does not occur. Only one Soul Bind family record may exist per identity; another failed-save application while still living/dying refreshes to the later pending endpoint without stacked prisons. No post-death recast is legal because the spell targets a living dying creature.
operational.scaling: None. No increased targets, indefinite duration or automatic save failure.
operational.limitations: Pending dispel/removal targets the creature. After death, existing remains serve as the local magical anchor for an otherwise eligible dispel/removal; if no remains exist, a source must expressly free the bound identity/soul rather than inventing a physical anchor. A generic cure or under-ranked dispel is not sufficient. The spell grants no commands, ownership, memories, personality change or control over the player. Soul-specific temporal restoration uses its own reviewed interface. Normal costs, Dissonance, Refrain and countering apply.
operational.designNotes: Core Necromancy rank9, 26RP, Action, 120ft, V/S/F and dying-target/resurrection-block purpose retained with Cleric/Druid/Wizard17 access. NEW: Charisma save,1-minute pending/24-hour bound states, no concentration, exact expiry collision, source-family refresh and local removal anchor. These replace the otherwise nonoperational Instantaneous summary with explicit finite aftermath. Wider soul cosmology remains open; individually reviewed for the operational playtest overlay.
